I might fear a butterfly would devour me whole, before I would I fear the brother of my soul.

I should wish to stop him. To protect him from this desire of his to do himself such harm.
I'm just concerned he might take it too far some day.
We need him in one piece.
I don't need to be worrying about having to clean up his corpse.
If there is one thing I know of Lyon to be certain, it is that he will always be there when he is needed.
You echo the words of the devil. Is it only callous need of capable hands that inspires you ?
Dégoûtant.
He is the great protector, le bouclier sacré de Lua.... The shining light in the darkness of the night.
No, I care about him a great deal. I just am worried when we need him, he won't be there.
I just need to know if I can count on him or not, or if he's already too broken.

The pain he inflicts upon himself... he does to hear his own thoughts. To feel his own body.
I wonder who will help you, when you are laid low and are in need of a hand.

For the sky is filled with stars, and each of them whisper to him, and he, like Lua herself, would be lost among them.
Or do you believe that time has already come and gone, and now you are above such reproach ?
And like Lua, he goes through his phases. He becomes consumed by the Void only to shine so bright that we all may walk in darkness without fear.
But like all blessings, it comes with a curse. Do I make any sense ? I fear I am only rambling.
I understand completely. And I have... a bit of a confession to make. [Confess feelings for Lyon.]
I understand what you're saying, but I can't condone him hurting himself. He should stop.
[Warning: Discussion of suicide.] I lost someone once, to that kind of self-harm. I can't... I can't condone it.
There has to be another way.
You're making perfect sense. I just... wish I could help him.

- for what condoléances could someone you barely know give, that could serve as a balm to a tragédie such as that ?
And for this, I cannot adore you more. But help form takes can be many things, non ?

No, it won't kill him. But it's still not okay.
I guess I see your point.
This soul you lost of which you speak... were they close to you ?
To help a baby bird may be to kill it. To help a candle flame may be to blow it out in your exubérance.
Oh, but this is such wonderful news !
I have found that being beside him when he needs me... listening to him, holding him when he weeps ?

Does more for him than speaking of what he should and should not do.

Does more for him than speaking of what he should and should not do.

Lost in the hallways of his mind again or paying attention to some other esprit in the room.

I told you that I was a beggar upon the streets, when I was a jeune fille. And that I did well for myself and that I had many friends.
I was born into a rich famille, which might surprise you. The bourgeois class, who are closer to the Orokin than not.
You must earn the trust of the stray. Let him come to you, non ? Does this make sense ?
One of them was a big older boy named Hugo.
But when I was born as I was... deformed, with mes pieds tordus et inutilisables ? Oh, ma mère could not have that.
Yes, actually. Thank you.
More than it should, thank you.
None. But thanks for trying.
He was a bit of the leader of the pack. And he always made sure no one picked on me and I had all I needed.
There were appearances to be maintained, oui ? Standards to be kept.
Bien ! I was afraid I let my metaphors get away from me again.
Marie and her metaphors. Ah, bon.
Mince alors. I knew I let my métaphores get away from me again.
He even helped me build des béquilles - you might call them... eh... crutches ? That I could use to drag myself about, with bits of wood we scavenged.
So, what was to be done, with poor malformed Marie ? I was brought to la Cité de la Lumière, where certainly I would parish upon the streets...
Hm. It occurs to me that perhaps describing Lyon as a stray dog is not the most flattering comparison to make...
One morning, we went to go wake him, and we found him -
And abandoned to die.
Perhaps do not tell him I did so, oui...?
Je... I will spare you the details... I am certain you can guess.
How old were you?
Your family left you for dead?

But he left us a note. It was barely legible. He was the only one of the other children who knew his letters, and I had to read it to the others.
Six ? Seven ? In their eyes, they had tried their best to mend me for many years. Tutors to teach me to walk. Braces. Footwear.
In their eyes, they had tried their best to mend me for many years. Tutors to teach me to walk. Braces. Footwear.
I think it's adorable, and so will he.
Your secret is safe with me.
I remember still how my voice choked. But I had to stay strong. Because even then, I knew that I had a duty to the others.
They were tired of the burden. So, barely able to even read and write my numbers and letters, I found myself in the muck.
Quelle horrible personne ! J'espère que votre chaise va s'effondrer et vous donner plein d'échardes douloureuses !
Merci ! What a relief...
Hugo had always seemed so happy to us, they said to me. Si joyeux. Always meeting life with a laugh and a sneer.
That's horrible.
How did you survive?

Chat ends.
Even when we were chased away or he was beaten with a stick for theft or loitering, it did not seem to bother him.

But we never know the depth of the pain others feel in their hearts. And in that letter, I knew he wept with Lua.
It was like you said, non ? All inconveniences come with a secret power.
true
What made me indésirable pour ma mère, made me quite popular amongst the other children of the streets.
false
But that he was now at peace at her side. For a time, I resented him for leaving. For the others looked to me for guidance. And I resented him for abandoning me.
What is more pathétique than a child with no pieds, oui ? I could earn more in a day with open palms than they could rob in a week.
But over time, I came to understand the truth of it.
And I was always wont to share. So I had many friends who would look out for me, take care of me. One of them was a big older boy named Hugo.
We can only forgive ourselves for being human. And forgive ourselves the pain of their leaving.
For it is their absence that hurts us. And the thought that we could not do more to aid them.
The burdens that others carry are never ours to know.
And that is a great tragédie. But it is what it means to be human.
I do not know if this story aided you. But I can only pray that it did. I must go, Monsieur Loid is calling.
Thank you, Marie.
[Stay silent.]
